title: Two forms, one space
say: Welcome back! You already know the cone and the cylinder. Today we will put them together. Watch how the cylinder passes through the cone, and how each form affects what we can see of the other. We will take our time with the new parts: perspective, overlap, and the shadows where they meet.

form affects what we can see of the other
We will take our time with the new parts
perspective overlap and the shadows where they meet

title: Keep your familiar tools nearby
say: Keep your pencils and eraser close by. Use light construction marks on your sketch paper, and leave space on both sides for the cylinder. We will spend less time repeating the basics today, and more time looking at how these two forms fit together.
hint: Light marks · Room on both sides

title: Place the whole drawing
say: Use the familiar centre and base guides. This time, leave extra space on the left and right. We are composing the whole combined object, not just a cone. Try that on your page. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Leave room for the cylinder on both sides.

title: A familiar cone framework
say: You have done this in the last lesson. Check the height, width and smooth base ellipse. Make any small correction you need. We are about to build across this framework. Take your time. I will wait for you.
hint: A short check, then something new.

title: Set the direction of the cylinder
say: These sloping guide lines set the direction and width of the cylinder. They are not a box in the finished drawing. Compare their tilt with the reference, and keep them light enough to change. Check the whole direction before shaping the ends. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.
hint: The box-like guides are a scaffold.

title: Turn the end into an ellipse
say: The circular end looks like an ellipse from this viewpoint. Compare its height, width and tilt with the teacher. It belongs to the sloping cylinder, so do not draw an unrelated upright oval. Shape it gently within the guides. Try that on your page. Continue when you are ready.
hint: A round end seen at an angle.

title: Check both ends together
say: Compare the two end ellipses and the long sides connecting them. They describe one cylinder passing across the cone. Check their alignment as a pair. Keep the hidden construction light for now. Take your time. I will wait for you.
hint: One cylinder, not two separate ovals.

title: Find where the surfaces meet
say: Look at the curved meeting line on the right. It shows where the cylinder emerges from the cone. This is not a straight cut across the page. Compare its curve with the reference and follow the two surfaces. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.

title: You are bringing the forms together
say: You have worked out how the two forms share the page. That careful looking is the important part. Relax your hand for a moment. Next, we will clear the hidden guides.

title: Erase only the hidden guides
say: The eraser is removing construction lines that would not show on the solid object. Before you rub, follow the line and ask: would I actually see this part? Lift it gently. Keep the outer edges and the curved meeting line. Take your time. I will wait for you.

say: Now the teacher marks the areas that will turn into shadow. Follow the cone and the cylinder separately, but keep one shared light direction. These are guides for changes in tone, not heavy outlines. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.

title: Begin with a clear dark family
say: Notice the first darker band on the cone. The teacher is establishing a clear value difference before adding all the middle tones. You know how to layer pencil marks. Here, compare the value across the whole object. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.

title: A cylinder casts onto the cone
say: Look beneath the projecting cylinder. It blocks light and casts a shadow onto the cone. That shadow helps the two forms feel connected. Compare its shape carefully; it is different from the shaded underside of the cylinder. Try that on your page. Continue when you are ready.
hint: The shadow belongs to the surface below it.

title: Connect the two visible ends
say: The teacher now develops the darker underside on the left. Compare it with the right-hand side. The cone hides the middle of the cylinder, but the visible ends should still feel part of one object. Take your time. I will wait for you.
hint: Both ends belong to the same form.

title: Anchor the object to the table
say: This wider shadow falls on the tabletop. Keep it connected to the base. Compare it with the smaller shadow on the cone: the two shadows fall on different surfaces. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.
hint: The cast shadow meets the base.

say: Look how the shadows connect the two shapes. This is more than drawing them side by side. You are making them belong in the same space. Keep going, one thoughtful adjustment at a time.

title: Turn the cylinder with tone
say: The teacher builds the round side with overlapping pencil marks. Keep the top lighter and the underside darker. Compare the transition rather than tracing a dark border around the cylinder. Try that on your page. Continue when you are ready.

title: Separate surface tone from cast shadow
say: Here, the shaded cylinder and the shadow on the cone sit close together. Keep looking at which surface each patch belongs to. Small value changes can separate them without a heavy outline. Take your time. I will wait for you.

title: Keep the cone turning
say: The teacher returns to the cone to balance its tones with the cylinder. This is a comparison step, not a new object. Keep the light area readable and build the middle tones gradually. Adjust what you need, then we will move on.

title: Compare the whole value pattern
say: Take a short step back. Can you still read the cone, the cylinder, and their meeting line? Keep the cylinder end distinct from its curved side. Adjust only what helps the forms become clearer. Try that on your page. Continue when you are ready.
hint: Check the forms before adding more dark.

title: A light pencil for small refinements
say: The teacher is using a two H pencil here for small adjustments near the join. Notice the light pressure. A harder pencil can help refine the transition, but it does not need to scratch a dark line into the paper. Take your time. I will wait for you.

say: You have built the forms, checked their perspective, and connected them with light and shadow. Your core drawing is complete. The background and extra finishing are optional. You can explore them, or share your work and move on.

say: The core drawing is already complete. If you want to explore the background, watch how tone beside the light edge helps it stand out. Keep these marks outside the object. You can skip this whole section. Take your time. I will wait for you.

title: Look for forms that meet
say: Look around for an object made from more than one simple form. Where does one part disappear behind another? Where does it cast a shadow? You now have a way to investigate that, one shape at a time.
hint: What would you build from two forms?

title: Two forms, one achievement
say: You stayed with a more complex drawing and worked out how its parts belong together. That deserves a celebration. Artchi has a reward for you. Next, we will take these skills into drawing a gift box.
